references.text: Earlier in the prologue, it is stated that "all things were made through him, and without him was not any thing made" ([ref:Joh 1:3|John 1:3]). Verse 10 repeats this motif: "the world was made through him" (ὁ κόσμος δι᾽ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο).

The creation account in [ref:1 Mos 1:1-3|Genesis 1:1-3] shows that God created all things through his word. John links the Logos directly to this act of creation by saying that the world was made through him.

The next verse ([ref:Joh 1:11|John 1:11]) expands on the rejection mentioned in verse 10: "He came to his own, and his own people did not receive him." The world's failure to recognize him is extended to the rejection by his own people.
In his high priestly prayer, Jesus says: "Righteous Father, the world has not known you" ([ref:Joh 17:25|John 17:25]). This reflects the motif from 1:10 that the world did not know him.

Paul confirms the creation motif: "For us there is ... one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things exist" ([ref:1 Kor 8:6|1 Corinthians 8:6]). This aligns with John 1:10's statement that the world was made through the Logos.

[ref:Kol 1:16-17|Colossians 1:16-17] teaches that "all things were created through him and for him", and that "he is before all things, and in him all things hold together". This cosmic Christology corresponds with John's statement that the world was made through the Logos.
[ref:Hebr 1:2|Hebrews 1:2] says that God "created the worlds by" the Son. This confirms the idea from John 1:10 that the world was created through Christ.
[ref:1 Joh 3:1|1 John 3:1] explains that "the world does not know us, because it did not know him". The world's lack of knowledge of Christ from John 1:10 also affects believers.

Isaiah laments: "The ox knows its owner ... but Israel does not know, my people do not understand" ([ref:Jes 1:3|Isaiah 1:3]). The theme that God's own people do not know him forms the background for John 1:10's statement that the world did not know the Logos.
Jesus says they persecute you "because they have not known the Father nor me" ([ref:Joh 16:3|John 16:3]). The world's hostility is due to its lack of knowledge – the same motif as in 1:10.

The wisdom in [ref:Ordsp 8:22-31|Proverbs 8:22-31] was with God before the world was created and acted as a "craftsman" during creation. John uses similar motifs regarding the Logos' role in creation and his presence in the world.
